newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya tea production rose in August.
newsitem.headline: Kenya tea production rose in August.

text.p: Production of Kenya's main commodity export tea rose in August despite adverse weather, a leading brokerage company said on Friday.
Mombasa-based African Tea Brokers (ATB) put August output at 18,344,022 kgs, up more than two million kg over August 1995.
In a report passed to Reuters, the brokerage said cumulative production for January-August was 170.02 million kgs, up 11.25 million kgs or 7.09 percent over the previous year.
"Kenya's main growing regions received seasonally high rainfall with very cold temperatures while severe widespread hail has been reported in Kericho and parts of Sotik," it said.
Kericho and Sotik are key growing areas in western Kenya.
The report said growth had been inhibited while hail in the the western region will cause future crop losses.

A total of five sales were held in September when 261,391 packages were sold for an average price of $1.45, compared to four sales in Septmber last year when a total of 186,193 packages were sold at an average $1.28, the report said.
Pakistan, Egypt, Sudan, Britain and Middle Eastern countries were the main buyers of Kenyan tea in the month. Two sales were also made to Somalia, the report said. --Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261
